cells.tense: You are reading what counts in this room, and the reading holds without a case built under it.
cells.act: put a date, a place, a container on it
cells.ask: Choose the conversation you keep circling and put a day, an hour and a place on it, then show up.
cells.core:
You read what counts before you can argue for it, and the read sits easy in you. You can stand in a room that hasn't settled yet and not rush it into sense. People leave you steadier than they came, though nobody has said why, and you don't either. When a thing between people is off, you feel its shape before you can name it, and the shape holds up.

What's left is to give that a container. Pick the thing you've already seen is the one to do — the conversation, the application, the visit — and give it a day and an hour. Structure won't tell you what to care about; it makes room for what you care about already. Keep it small: a time written down, a place agreed. Your read is the thing itself; a container means it happens.
cells.sheetLine: You read what counts. Give it a day and a place.
cells.verb: seeing what counts before you can argue for it
cells.place: where things between people get set back into proportion

cells.tense: You will have read every corner of this before you let it stand anywhere.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Go one step toward the outcome you'd miss most, taken while the doubt keeps talking, before you've finished weighing it.
cells.core:
You read what counts before you argue for it, and something in you is trying to earn that read — one more source, one more version, the picture kept open until it's certainly right. Going well, this looks like a person who can sit with an unfinished question and still move: enough signal to act, no case required. The reading goes on after the signal has arrived.

Take the aim you actually want and move toward it, plainly, before you can justify it. One step on the way will do, taken while the doubt keeps talking. Let something stay unfinished and go anyway. What you've built up in private needs somewhere to land, and landing is what settles it.
cells.sheetLine: You've read enough. Move before it's certain.

cells.tense: You used to trust your read on things, and now you hold it up for someone else to confirm.
cells.act: picture it a year on, turned out well, and keep the picture
cells.ask: Let an unsettled situation come out well a year from now, seen in plain detail; hold that picture a day before asking anyone.
cells.core:
Your own read has been overruled so often that you don't trust it now, and you carry it to somebody else to be told it's allowed. The read isn't gone. It's waiting for permission from outside. You still have a take on things — that part of you is tired, not blind.

Don't try to force the certainty back. Let an uncertain situation come out well a year from now, in ordinary detail — where you are, what's been settled. Keep that picture a day, in private, before you check it against anyone. The read comes back on a small piece of ground, not by meeting the whole fog head-on.
cells.sheetLine: Your read is still there. Don't hand it over to be confirmed.

cells.tense: You keep arriving at decisions that fit, and you keep filing them under luck.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: Settle a favor you owe, or take back what you've let someone keep, and square that one account.
cells.core:
Your read on what counts is running the show and keeping its name off the bill. A choice you'd call instinct is you, taking the room's measure before the argument, and the choice usually comes out right. You watch the same thing happen again and wonder where it came from. It's the same place it has been.

Give it a small, plain place at the table. One exchange between you and someone else, set level — what you owe given back, what's yours taken up. One scale, not a settlement; nothing after it. Small deal, done, and you've had your hand on something fair without needing to say why it's fair. That's all it needed.
cells.sheetLine: The clean calls you credit to luck are yours.
